Future work

Source: ROADMAP.md

Proposed additions to bicountbrms, not yet scheduled. Each entry states the change and the design questions it raises. Move an entry to NEWS.md when it is released.

Both parameterisations in the articles

Getting started introduces both parameterisations. The articles would give each formula, prior and summary in both the congruence–bias coordinates and the native parameters, as tabs (## Heading {.tabset} in R Markdown, which pkgdown renders).

  • Decide whether each congruence–bias tab fits its own model, which adds one fit per tab to the precompile, or converts the posterior draws of the native fit.
  • Priors written on one scale induce a different density on the other, so the two tabs are not the same model unless the prior is converted as well.

Zero inflation

Excess zeros in one or both observed counts, beyond those implied by the negative-binomial components.

  • Decide where the zero process acts: on each observed count separately, on the shared component, or on the pair (a structural zero for both counts). These are three different models, and only the last one leaves the shared component interpretable as a count recorded by both sources.
  • A zero-inflation probability is a new distributional parameter, which changes the lpmf signature for every constructor that gains it.

Both sources partially observed

At present only the first count may be unrecorded. Allowing the second to be unrecorded as well adds a third kind of row, in which only the first count is observed, scored by the marginal of the first count.

  • The observation indicators would become two vint() integers, so the plain constructors would pass two literals ("1", "1") rather than one. Every constructor changes its vars, and tests/testthat/test-stancode-shape.R must be updated for all four.
  • .y1_obs_at() in R/utils.R generalises to a lookup for either indicator, and new functions posterior_predict_y2_given_y1() and posterior_epred_y2_given_y1() would impute y_2 on rows where only y_1 was recorded.
  • The split between the shared and exclusive components is estimated mainly from the paired rows, as it is now, so the number of paired rows remains the effective sample size for the bias and the congruence.

Citation section in the README

The Citation section was removed from README.md on 14 November 2026, before the paper describing the package was submitted to Methods in Ecology and Evolution, because the reviewers receive an anonymised copy of the repository. Restore the Citation section once the paper is published.

  • Point the restored section and inst/CITATION to the paper, and keep the citation("bicountbrms") call and the concept DOI (10.5281/zenodo.22239120).
  • Add Kirkpatrick (2022) to the citHeader in inst/CITATION, which at present cites Holgate (1964), Karlis and Ntzoufras (2003), and Kirkpatrick and Neale (2016).
